darkMode.label: Dark mode
darkMode.description: Switch between light and dark UI themes.

mode.label: Mode
mode.description: Choose system, light, or dark appearance. Some terminal themes are dark-only.

themePack.label: Theme colors
themePack.description: Applies to ThreadTerm chrome, session cards, floating terminals, and the xterm palette.

descriptions.threadterm-default: The native ThreadTerm blue theme and stable fallback.
descriptions.acme-mono: Monochrome editorial surfaces with crisp borders and a restrained terminal palette.
descriptions.catppuccin: Soft pastel surfaces with a calm terminal palette.
descriptions.gruvbox: Warm retro colors tuned for long terminal sessions.
descriptions.everforest: Green-tinted low-contrast surfaces for reduced glare.
descriptions.dracula: A vivid dark terminal theme with purple and pink accents.
descriptions.github-primer: GitHub-inspired neutrals with strong terminal readability.
descriptions.one-dark: Atom-inspired dark editor colors with a balanced ANSI palette.
descriptions.night-owl: A blue night palette tuned for readable long-running terminals.
descriptions.ayu: Warm minimal surfaces with contrast-adjusted terminal colors.
descriptions.nord: Arctic blue-gray surfaces with soft but legible accents.
descriptions.rose-pine: Muted rose and pine tones with clearer terminal contrast.
descriptions.kanagawa: Ink-wash colors adapted for session cards and terminals.
descriptions.solarized-contrast: Solarized-inspired hues with stronger foreground contrast.

dataIO.title: Settings import and export
dataIO.description: Move ThreadTerm preferences, custom themes, and overlay hotkeys with one safe JSON file.
dataIO.previewDescription: Choose which sections should overwrite your current setup.
dataIO.safetyHint: Bridge tokens, paired devices, audit logs, provider keys, cards, and terminal output are never exported.

dataDirectory.title: ThreadTerm data location
dataDirectory.description: Choose where ThreadTerm keeps its own database, interface state, and window state. Projects and Agent data are never moved.
dataDirectory.desktopOnly: Data location management is available in the desktop app.
dataDirectory.chooseTitle: Choose an empty ThreadTerm data folder
dataDirectory.boundary: Agent sessions, credentials, projects, repositories, and worktrees stay where they are.

pointer.label: Startup location pointer
pointer.description: This tiny file stays in the system configuration folder so ThreadTerm can find your selected data folder before it starts.

platform.macos: macOS keeps WebKit engine caches in a system-managed location. ThreadTerm business data still moves to your selected folder.

phases.scheduled: Ready to move after ThreadTerm closes.
phases.copying_to_staging: Copying data into a safe temporary area.
phases.pointer_switched: The new folder is active and awaiting confirmation.
phases.first_launch_confirmed: The new folder started successfully. The old copy is still retained.
phases.old_data_cleanup: The retained old data has been removed.
phases.rollback_to_source: The previous folder will be restored after restart.

preflight.ready: This folder is ready for migration.

move.title: Move ThreadTerm data
move.description: Choose a new or empty folder. The actual copy starts only after ThreadTerm has closed.

retain.label: Keep the old data copy after migration
retain.description: Recommended. You can verify the new folder, then delete the old copy manually from this page.

schedule.success: Migration is scheduled. Your current terminals will keep running until you close ThreadTerm.

restart.title: Restart ThreadTerm
restart.confirm: ThreadTerm will close and reopen. {{count}} open terminal(s) will be ended. Continue?
restart.starting: Restarting ThreadTerm to move the data…

rollback.title: Restore previous data folder
rollback.confirm: Use the retained previous data folder after the next restart? The current folder will not be deleted.
rollback.success: The previous folder will be restored when ThreadTerm restarts.

cleanup.title: Delete old ThreadTerm data
cleanup.confirm: Permanently delete the retained old ThreadTerm data at {{path}}? This cannot be undone.
cleanup.success: The retained old ThreadTerm data was deleted.

cache.title: Rebuildable desktop cache
cache.description: Browser-engine cache can be rebuilt and currently uses {{size}}. Cards, settings, database records, and login data are not included.
cache.systemManaged: macOS manages WebKit engine cache outside the selectable ThreadTerm data folder.
cache.pending: Cleanup is scheduled for the next time ThreadTerm starts.
cache.scheduled: Rebuildable cache will be cleared after ThreadTerm fully closes.
cache.cancelled: The pending cache cleanup was cancelled.

legacyPrompt.title: Choose one place for ThreadTerm data
legacyPrompt.description: This installation still uses older, separate folders. You can consolidate ThreadTerm data when convenient; terminals and Agent data will not be moved now.

notifications.title: System notifications
notifications.description: ThreadTerm sends OS notifications when a session needs input, hits an error, or finishes a reply.
notifications.devModeHint: In development mode, macOS may not list the source as ThreadTerm. Packaged builds use the ThreadTerm app identity.
notifications.desktopOnly: System notifications are only available in the Tauri desktop app.
notifications.sent: Sent to the OS notification service. If no banner appears, check your system notification settings or verify with a packaged build.
notifications.failed: Send failed. Check the development logs for details.
notifications.testBody: If you see this notification, the system notification path is working.

preference.title: Notification delivery
preference.description: Allow ThreadTerm to send system notifications for session events.

mobileAccess.title: Mobile access
mobileAccess.description: The service listens only on this computer. Phones must connect through a mature HTTPS tunnel such as Tailscale Serve or Cloudflare Tunnel.
mobileAccess.desktopOnly: Mobile access can only be started inside the Tauri desktop app.
mobileAccess.pairingDescription: Generate a five-minute, one-time pairing QR code over an HTTPS address and bind it to this computer identity.
mobileAccess.pairingStoppedDescription: Start mobile access and the 5-minute pairing QR code will appear here.
mobileAccess.pairingUnavailable: The QR code is not available yet. Generate a new pairing code to retry.

publishHost.label: HTTPS secure tunnel URL
publishHost.hint: Enter the complete HTTPS URL from Tailscale Serve, Cloudflare Tunnel, or another trusted tunnel. Leaving it empty supports local testing only.
publishHost.secureRequired: Phone pairing is not available yet. Enter an HTTPS secure tunnel URL and generate a new pairing code.

permissionMode.label: Pairing permission
permissionMode.hint: Full control can type into live sessions from the paired device.

account.languageDescription: Choose the display language for ThreadTerm.

supervisorSettings.enableHint: Watch pinned cards for prompts that need your attention.
supervisorSettings.howItWorksBody: When a pinned card pauses on a sudo prompt, [y/N] confirmation, AI question, or arrow-select menu, ThreadTerm fires a notification. Click it to focus the card and reply in the terminal.
